title: Coproduct encoding and fpqc cover for family scheme descent
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be a set, and let $\{f_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site]. Fix a family scheme descent datum $(V_i\to T_i,\phi_{ij})$ [def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum], where $\phi_{ij}:V_i\times_TT_j\simeq T_i\times_TV_j$ satisfies the triple-overlap cocycle. Form $A=\coprod_iT_i$, $Z=\coprod_iV_i$ and the induced maps $f:A\to T$, $v:Z\to A$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Fibre products are as in [def-pc-fibre-product], with all families and coproducts in the fixed universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. There is a singleton descent datum $D$ on $v$ relative to $f$ [def-pd-descent-datum] with the following properties. The canonical identifications
$$A\times_TA\cong\coprod_{i,j}(T_i\times_TT_j),\quad Z\times_TA\cong\coprod_{i,j}(V_i\times_TT_j),\quad A\times_TZ\cong\coprod_{i,j}(T_i\times_TV_j)$$
and their triple-product versions identify the transport of $D$ with $\coprod_{i,j}\phi_{ij}$ and its cocycle with the given component cocycles. Restricting $D$ to the coproduct components recovers the original family datum. The singleton $\{f:A\to T\}$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], also when $I$ is infinite. For every $T$-scheme $W$, there exists an isomorphism $W\times_TA\simeq Z$ over $A$ identifying the canonical datum with $D$ if and only if there exist isomorphisms $W\times_TT_i\simeq V_i$ compatible with all $\phi_{ij}$. Thus the family datum is effective if and only if $D$ is effective; the same scheme $W/T$ realizes both. The assertion includes the empty covering of the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 023X, lemma-family-is-one, construction and restriction to components; the fpqc assertion uses Topologies Tag 021P, lemma-fppf-affine, with Tag 022B, definition-fpqc-covering.

proof.text: For a family with an existing coproduct, its nonempty support is small: choose a point in each nonempty summand; coprojections inject these chosen points into the coproduct. Injectivity follows by mapping the coproduct to its disjoint binary double, sending one summand left and all the others right. Restrict the universal cofan to this small support; empty summands have unique outgoing maps. The small-family scheme coproduct theorem then gives open coprojections, disjointness and coverage for the original family [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. This also applies to every colimiting cofan by its unique comparison isomorphism.

Pull back an arbitrary colimiting scheme cofan. Its legs remain open immersions and their ranges are the inverse images of the old ranges, by the open fibre-product geometry [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]. They are disjoint and cover. Restriction to the small nonempty support and the scheme disjoint-open-cofan theorem show that this is again a colimit. Thus scheme coproduct cofans are universal. Apply Mathlib IsUniversalColimit.nonempty_isColimit_prod_of_pullbackCone to the two canonical coproduct cofans to obtain the canonical pair cofan. Apply it again to this pair cofan and the third family to obtain the triple cofan. The legs are exactly the specified pullback.map morphisms [def-pc-fibre-product].

Convert the represented local sheaf points to morphisms over each component and conjugate the given transitions to localTransport [def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum]. Its identity and cocycle are the corresponding descent-data laws; its naturality follows from pullHom_hom, the transition naturality square and naturality of the representing bijections. On each component V_i times_T U_j, apply localTransport to the first projection and include its result in V_j. The pair cofan from the preceding step glues these morphisms into a single familyAction. Its composite with Z to A is the second projection, by coproduct uniqueness and the local transport structure equation.

For a point x over a:B to A and b:B to A with equal image in T, define transport by the lift (x,b) into Z times_T A followed by familyAction. Pullback universality gives naturality. A map to a coproduct locally factors through its components; iterating the universal cofan argument gives jointly epimorphic decompositions for two or three such maps. The square over a component of A is Cartesian because the coprojections are open immersions and their disjoint ranges show that the inverse image of U_i is V_i. Thus a local restriction of x lifts uniquely to V_i. On such components the assembled transport is exactly localTransport, by its naturality and the cofan desc equation. Its identity and cocycle now follow from the corresponding local laws, using the jointly epimorphic decompositions. This constructs D [def-pd-descent-datum] and proves its stated component restriction equation, including the specified represented-point conventions.

The coprojections form an open cover of A even when the original index type is not small, by the support argument above. Flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism] and local finite presentation are Zariski local at source, so the equations iota_i followed by Sigma.desc f = f_i and the fppf hypotheses imply both properties of Sigma.desc f. Joint surjectivity is immediate by including a preimage in its summand. Thus the singleton is itself fppf [def-pc-fppf-site]; Mathlib Scheme.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage gives its fpqc membership [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. No finite affine refinement lemma is needed.

Fix W/T. Restrict q:Z to W along the coprojections; the component square is Cartesian by pasting its Cartesian inclusion square with the global square. Conversely form q by Sigma.desc of the local q_i. Mathlib IsUniversalColimit.isPullback_of_isColimit_left, applied to the universal cofan of the U_i and the colimiting cofan of the V_i, proves the global square Cartesian. Global invariance implies local invariance by the represented component equation. Conversely, restrict two test maps and a point to their component decomposition; the transport restriction formula and the local invariance equation give global invariance by coproduct uniqueness. This proves the fixed-W equivalence. Existentially quantify W and unfold the two geometric effectivity definitions [def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum, def-pd-descent-datum]. Empty index types and empty summands need no extra case: the support constructions use initiality of empty schemes and all cofan universal properties, covers and equality tests remain valid.

proof_origin.place: Tag 023X, lemma-family-is-one; formalized by universal scheme cofans and represented-point transports. The fpqc clause uses Mathlib Scheme.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage after establishing that the coproduct singleton is fppf.
